key_insight: Latent-WAM learns a compact, spatially-aware and dynamics-informed latent world that enables accurate end-to-end trajectory planning with far lower data and compute requirements than prior world-model planners.
problem_solved: Existing world-model-based driving planners produce overly large or spatially-agnostic representations and underuse temporal dynamics, leading to sub-optimal planning under constrained data and compute budgets.
method: Spatially-aware latent encoder: compress multimodal sensor inputs into a compact latent world that preserves geometric layout and agent context.
Dynamics-informed temporal model: learn latent-space transition dynamics for multi-step prediction and planning, improving foresight and robustness.
Joint end-to-end planner: decode planned trajectories and controls from latent world states with lightweight inference and planning-aware losses.
impact: Offers a practical blueprint for building sample- and compute-efficient end-to-end driving systems, improving planning robustness and lowering deployment cost for autonomous driving and other embodied agents.
visual_elements: System architecture diagram: sensors → spatial latent encoder → latent dynamics module → planner → vehicle controls
Side-by-side visualization: raw sensor/BEV inputs vs compact spatial latent map to show compression and geometric fidelity
Trajectory rollout comparisons: predicted vs ground-truth trajectories under occlusion/limited-data scenarios
Efficiency plot: compute/inference-time vs planning error (ADE/FDE) demonstrating Latent-WAM gains
paper_title: Latent-WAM: Latent World Action Modeling for End-to-End Autonomous Driving
paper_authors: Linbo Wang, Yupeng Zheng, Qiang Chen, Shiwei Li, Yichen Zhang
